newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian gov't ministers quit in radio scandal.
newsitem.headline: Colombian gov't ministers quit in radio scandal.

text.p: Two top Colombian government ministers resigned on Tuesday after becoming embroiled in a political scandal sparked by allegations they illegally awarded radio broadcast licenses to cronies of President Ernesto Samper.

Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar, who was appointed in July 1995, and Communications Minister Saulo Arboleda, who took office in August last year, quit one day after the weekly political magazine Semana published the accusations of corruption.
The article, which hit newsstands on Monday, reproduced excerpts of a taped conversation between the pair in which they discussed how to divide up 81 FM radio contracts to the president's friends.
The revelations generated a political backlash and led the ruling Liberal Party, to whom both ministers belong, to call for their resignation early on Tuesday.
Colombia's Chief Prosecutor Alfonso Gomez and Attorney General Jaime Bernal have launched a criminal investigation into how the licenses were awarded.
There was no immediate comment on the resignations from the president's office. Texts of the resignation letters were not immediately available.
